identity.title: Mapping Circumstellar Magnetic Fields of Late-type Evolved Stars with the Goldreich-Kylafis Effect: CARMA Observations at λ1.3 mm of R Crt and R Leo

paper_type_evidence.quote: we present the detection of spectral-line polarization from both the thermal $J=2-1$ CO line and the $v=1, J=5-4$ SiO maser line toward two thermal-pulsating (TP-) AGB stars, R Crt and R Leo.
The gain calibrator absolute flux densities were obtained from high-quality ALMA band 6 ($211 - 275$ GHz) calibrator catalogue[^2] entries adjacent in time.

distance_source.value: P-L distance from Matthews et al. 2018

question.value: Can Goldreich-Kylafis linear polarization of thermal CO J=2-1 be detected with CARMA toward R Crt and R Leo, and is it consistent with G-K model predictions for the circumstellar magnetic field?

evidence.quote: In this section we describe numerical modeling to determine if this linear polarization can be ascribed to the G-K effect.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Narrow windows 62.2 MHz, 191 channels (0.453 and 0.423 km/s); two 489.6 MHz continuum windows

evidence.quote: Both lines were observed in narrow-band (line) spectral windows of bandwidth $\triangle \nu = 62.2$ MHz each sampled over $191$ frequency channels
with adopted transition rest frequencies of 215.596 GHz and 230.538 GHz respectively
with adopted transition rest frequencies of 215.596 GHz and 230.538 GHz respectively
The observations of R Crt and R Leo were performed in the CARMA E-configuration ($8.5 - 66$ m baseline lengths).
At $230$ GHz, the beam size is $5.73'' \times 4.21''$ (at PA $=29.7^{\circ}$) for the calibrated R Crt data and $5.07'' \times 3.58''$ (at PA = $80.1^{\circ}$) for the calibrated R Leo data.
Two observing runs were performed, on November 16, 2014 and November 11, 2014 respectively, with each run of total duration 3.7 hours.

provided.value: Full-Stokes 1.3 mm observations of CO and SiO

evidence.quote: The correlator was configured in full Stokes mode to observe the SiO $v=1, J=5-4$ line in the lower sideband (LSB) and the CO $J = 2-1$ line in the upper sideband (USB)

provided.value: Band 6 flux densities of gain calibrators

evidence.quote: The resulting flux densities were $8.38 \pm 0.39$ Jy (3C279) and $3.04 \pm 0.17$ Jy (OJ287).

what.value: CSE parameters for R Leo (Mdot, v_inf, Rc, beta) from Danilovich et al. 2015

evidence.quote: We adopt an inner dust condensation radius $R_{c} \sim 1.6 \times 10^{14}\ \rm{cm}$ from SED modeling (cite: success15).

method.value: Yang & Lai G-K code with mixed 1-D/2-D LVG geometry, optionally with anisotropic radiation from central star

evidence.quote: A mixed LVG velocity gradient geometry (Fig. [8](#fig:COpol_model_LVGs)(iii)) was adopted in the G-K modeling

assumptions.value: Uniform magnetic field and velocity gradient in constant-density slab

evidence.quote: The model used here considers an uniform magnetic field and uniform velocity gradient through the slab of material with constant thickness and density, as a first-order approximation.

validation.value: Compared predicted m_l with observed CO polarization

evidence.loc: Observed linear polarization and the G-K model predictions
evidence.quote: Our G-K model predicts $m_l \sim 3\%$ (Fig. [7](#fig:COpol_model)) which is consistent with our observational result for the CO emission toward R Crt.

results_numeric.quantity: SiO maser linear polarization R Crt / R Leo

evidence.quote: We detect linear polarization in the $v=1,\ J=5-4$ SiO maser emission toward R Crt at $m_l \sim 17.2\%$ and R Leo at $m_l\sim 34.6\%$
We detect continuum emission toward R Crt of $14.9 \pm 2.4$ mJy/beam in the LSB continuum spectral window
We detect peak fractional circular polarization $m_c \sim 5.7\%$ in the $v=1, J=5-4$ SiO maser line toward R Leo

findings_qualitative.value: G-K model with anisotropic radiation cannot readily produce m_l > 5%, so R Leo's 9.7% needs additional effects

evidence.loc: Observed linear polarization and the G-K model predictions
evidence.quote: we find that a fractional linear polarization exceeding $m_l > 5\%$ cannot readily be generated by our G-K model including anisotropic radiation.
No continuum polarization was detected toward either R Crt or R Leo

claims.hypothesis: CO J=2-1 linear polarization in R Crt and R Leo arises from the G-K effect
claims.experiment: CARMA full-Stokes observations compared with G-K model using a semi-analytic CSE
claims.result: Model predicts ~3%; observed 3.13% (R Crt) and 9.7% (R Leo)
claims.finding: Consistent for R Crt; R Leo exceeds the model, so additional effects needed

evidence.quote: The observed thermal line polarization level is consistent with the predicted results from the G-K model for R Crt; additional effects need to be considered for R Leo.

claims.hypothesis: SiO maser lines are linearly and circularly polarized in these stars
claims.result: m_l 17-34%; circular only toward R Leo
claims.finding: Maser polarization detected, broadly consistent with earlier J=2-1 results

evidence.quote: We also have detected linear polarization in the $v=1, J=5-4$ SiO maser line toward the CSE of R Crt and R Leo in the range $m_l \sim 17-34\%$.

why_this_method.value: G-K effect traces field morphology at depth, distinct from dust polarization and Zeeman

evidence.quote: The G-K polarization signal also arises from underlying physics that is distinct from the generating mechanisms for continuum dust polarization and the Zeeman effect.

limitations_admitted.value: Observations are sensitivity-limited; interferometric filtering may overestimate m_l

evidence.quote: These observations are profoundly sensitivity-limited compared to modern telescopes such as ALMA

referee_caveats_inferred: Data are CARMA, not ALMA; ALMA only supplies calibrator fluxes
G-K model uses slab with uniform field; only R Leo CSE modeled explicitly
Absolute EVPA systematic error ~11 deg and weak leakage correlation

data_public_as_stated.value: CARMA archival data referenced only for a comparison dataset; target data availability not stated
